groups.instructions: Complete the table below. Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage for each answer.
groups.strategy: Tables are read row by row. Use the column headings to predict what kind of information is missing.

questions.prompt: Hydroponics — roots are placed in a nutrient-rich ________.
questions.explanation: Paragraph B: 'roots sit in a nutrient-rich water solution'.

questions.prompt: Aeroponics — roots hang in the air and receive a ________.
questions.explanation: Paragraph B: 'sprayed with a fine mist'.

questions.prompt: Lighting — LED lamps mainly produce red and ________ light.
Climate control — temperature, humidity and ________ are managed by computer.
questions.explanation: Paragraph B: 'Temperature, humidity and carbon dioxide levels are controlled by computer'.

groups.instructions: Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO advantages of vertical farming are mentioned in paragraph C?
groups.strategy: Each correct letter scores one mark, in any order. Check every option against the text — two options will be mentioned elsewhere or not at all.

options.text: lower construction costs than conventional farms
reduced use of chemicals to control pests
lower energy consumption than field agriculture
much greater efficiency in the use of water
the ability to grow staple cereal crops

questions.explanation: B: 'little need for pesticides'. D: 'up to 95 per cent less water'. A and C are the opposite (paragraph D: high construction costs, energy is the greatest obstacle). E is contradicted in paragraph E.

groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information given in the passage? Write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.

questions.prompt: A vertically farmed lettuce always has a smaller carbon footprint than an imported one.
questions.explanation: Paragraph D: if electricity comes from fossil fuels, its footprint 'can actually exceed' that of a transported field lettuce. 'Always' is contradicted.

questions.prompt: Some vertical farming businesses have closed because of high energy costs.
questions.explanation: Paragraph D: several companies 'have gone out of business … after rising energy prices made their operations unprofitable'.

questions.prompt: Spinach is the most profitable crop grown in vertical farms.
questions.explanation: Spinach is listed as ideal, but no comparison of profitability between crops is made.

questions.prompt: Vertical farming is likely to become the world's main source of calories.
questions.explanation: Paragraph E: 'unlikely to replace conventional agriculture as the main source of the world's calories'.

groups.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct ending, A–E.

options.text: because they mature quickly and take up little space.
because importing fresh food there is already costly.
because they need long periods of intense light.
because supermarkets refuse to buy them.
because produce reaches shops very soon after harvest.

questions.prompt: Leafy greens are well suited to vertical farms
questions.explanation: Paragraph E: 'they grow quickly, are compact'.

questions.prompt: Wheat and rice are expensive to grow indoors
questions.explanation: Paragraph E: 'They take months to mature, need large amounts of light'.

questions.prompt: Vertical farms may be competitive in desert regions
questions.explanation: Paragraph F: 'the cost of importing fresh vegetables is already high'.
questions.trap: E is a real advantage (paragraph C) but it is not the reason given for desert regions.
